article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Cases surpassed 3,500 in Congo.
article.articleSummary:
- Over 3,532 laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases and 1,556 deaths have been reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo within about two and a half months, amid the 17th outbreak in the country. The epicenter is Ituri province in the northeast, adjoining South Sudan and Uganda, where roughly 90% of cases have occurred. Transmission is mainly via contact with bodily fluids and funeral practices; healthcare workers face elevated risk. The Bundibugyo strain has no vaccine or cure today. The outbreak was declared on May 15. The epidemic has spilled into four other provinces, including North Kivu and South Kivu, whose capitals are controlled by M23 rebels. Violence in Ituri from the ADF has killed many civilians (over 30). Uganda has announced the end of its outbreak, but WHO cautions ongoing risk.

Security challenges and reduced foreign aid in eastern DR Congo hinder containment, with access and contact tracing severely limited. article.articleHeadline: Sesau guides the public on Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease.
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) awareness campaign by Alagoinhas’ Sesau, Brazil, educates the public on HFMD care. HFMD is highly contagious, caused by enteroviruses (notably Coxsackieviruses), affecting mainly children under five and infants. Transmission occurs via direct contact or contaminated objects, making rapid recognition crucial to prevent daycare and school outbreaks. Incubation is 3–7 days; illness lasts 7–10 days. Common symptoms include fever, sore throat, malaise, loss of appetite, painful mouth ulcers, and small blisters or red spots on the palms and soles, possibly on buttocks, legs, or genital area. No vaccine exists; prevention relies on strict hygiene and respiratory etiquette: frequent handwashing with soap or 70% alcohol, do not share cups, utensils, pacifiers, bottles, towels, or toys; clean shared surfaces. Sick children should stay home until fever and active lesions resolve and medical clearance is obtained. Treatment is symptomatic: rest, fluids, soft foods, and prescribed analgesics.

article.articleHeadline: Molecular Diagnostics Becomes an Ally Against Avian Diseases - Agro in Field
article.articleSummary: Brazilian diagnostics firm Loccus, led by Tatiani Janegitz, highlights how molecular diagnostics, especially real-time PCR, enable early detection of infectious agents in poultry before clinical signs appear, guiding rapid responses and strengthening biosafety and sanitary programs. The ongoing threat of highly pathogenic avian influenza has underscored the value of surveillance to anticipate circulation, mutations, and dissemination routes, improving risk assessment and control decisions. This approach transforms disease management from reactive to continuous monitoring, reducing losses and supporting export markets. Beyond avian influenza, tests now aid detection of brucellosis, bovine tuberculosis, leptospirosis, mastitis, and neonatal diarrhea, aligning with international sanitary standards. The strategy emphasizes permanent surveillance in Brazilian poultry production to safeguard supply chains and animal health.

article.articleHeadline: Influenza remains at an elevated level with a positivity rate of 28.5%.
article.articleSummary: Influenza remains elevated in Brazil, with a 28.5% positivity rate in Epidemiological Week 28 (July 12–18, 2026), nearly three times higher than 10.2% in the same week of 2025. The five-week moving average stays around 27%, signaling stable, ongoing high transmission rather than a decline. Brazilian pathologist Dr. Carlos Eduardo Ferreira notes the virus remains widely circulating and urges continued epidemiological monitoring and preventive measures. Vaccination and laboratory diagnosis are emphasized as essential strategies to reduce severe cases and differentiate influenza from other respiratory infections, enabling faster clinical decisions and better public health planning. Data come from Abramed’s network; compiled via METRICARE by Controllab and shared with RNDS/DATASUS for national surveillance of respiratory diseases in Brazil. The article highlights the need to protect high-risk groups during the upcoming peak period for respiratory viruses.

article.articleHeadline: Toxin Produced by Bacteria Could Revolutionize the Fight Against Infections, According to a Study by the University of São Paulo
article.articleSummary: RhsF, a toxin produced by Chromobacterium violaceum, found in tropical regions and capable of causing severe infections in humans, could revolutionize antimicrobial therapy. The protein acts as a bacterial weapon during competition, delivered into rival cells via Type VI Secretion System, reducing or eliminating competitors. In the absence of RhsF, Chromobacterium violaceum shows reduced ability to suppress competitors. The toxin modifies RNA in target bacteria, an underexplored mechanism that may reveal new therapeutic targets against resistant infections. While promising, the work remains early-stage, with researchers pursuing the exact RNA substrates and how modifications lead to growth arrest or death. They identified the protective protein and determined the structure of the toxin-protective-protein complex, a key step for biotech applications. The study from USP Ribeirão Preto (FMRP), Brazil, published in Journal of Biological Chemistry, highlights microbial strategies for future medicine.

article.articleHeadline: Niterói is a reference in the use of the Wolbachia method to combat dengue | Niterói | O Dia
article.articleSummary: Wolbachia-based dengue control in Niterói, Brazil, highlighted at the 78th SBPC meeting. Initiated in 2015 in the Jurujuba neighborhood, the program achieved 100% city coverage by 2023 and is now deployed in 16 Brazilian cities, protecting about 5 million people. Internationally, the technology is used in 15 countries, benefiting more than 16 million people. Wolbachia bacteria, absent in Aedes aegypti, reduces transmission of dengue, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever and is self-sustaining as infected females pass it to offspring. In Niterói, 92% community approval supported releases, with studies showing an 89% decline in dengue cases after full-city coverage. The effort exemplifies translating research into a public-health tool and is expanding within Brazil’s national arbovirus prevention and control strategies, driven by science, monitoring, and community engagement.

article.articleHeadline: DRC: Julien Paluku mobilizes the BUREC to strengthen the Ebola response.
article.articleSummary: DRC political party Bloc Uni pour la Renaissance et l'Émergence du Congo (BUREC) mobilizes to strengthen the Ebola virus disease response in Ituri and North Kivu, tapping national MPs and a senator during parliamentary holidays to intensify community awareness campaigns. The plan emerged from a July 30, 2026 Kinshasa strategy meeting of the party’s Political Directorate, chaired by Julien Paluku Kahongya, addressing security and health in North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri, and organizing preparations for BUREC’s third congress. article.articleHeadline: International Rangers Day: warning about zoonotic risks faced by Congolese ecoguards - ACP
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, July 31, 2026 — On International Rangers Day, wildlife health experts warn that rangers are exposed to major zoonotic diseases during patrols, including Ebola, Marburg, Mpox, rabies, anthrax, brucellosis, and leptospirosis, plus vector-borne malaria and yellow fever. Risk rises when handling sick or dead animals, collecting samples, or operating in outbreak zones. They call for stronger biosafety measures and enhanced epidemiological surveillance to limit spillover between wildlife and people. Rangers use PPE, frequent handwashing, equipment disinfection, and safe waste disposal; they are trained to spot signs of disease in wildlife, report unusual die-offs, and avoid contact with carcasses. Vaccination, malaria prevention, and regular medical follow-up supplement protection. Advocates urge increased investment in ranger health, as ecoguards are frontline defenders of biodiversity and health surveillance in protected areas. Published July 31, 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola patient in Frankfurt cured: University Hospital reports discharge.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola patient infected in the Democratic Republic of Congo, later treated and discharged in Frankfurt, Germany. The patient carried the Bundibugyo variant. He arrived at Universitätsmedizin Frankfurt two weeks after exposure; treated on a specialized high-containment isolation unit. He remained stable and recovered under intensive supportive care: circulatory stabilization, fluid and electrolyte management, pain and symptom control, ongoing laboratory and vital-parameter monitoring. There is no vaccine or variant-specific therapy for Bundibugyo Ebola; treatment relies on meticulous supportive care. The infection source was a logistics worker for a humanitarian organization in DRC, highlighting exposure risk through contact with body fluids. The case emphasizes the importance of strict isolation, controlled patient transport, waste handling, PPE and interface management to prevent cross-contamination. Although Europe rarely sees Ebola, the Congo outbreak context remains hard to control, underlining reliance on non-specific supportive measures and infection-control readiness.

article.articleHeadline: DRC: the PNLT warns of an imminent shortage of medicines and inputs for tuberculosis.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) faces an imminent shortage of tuberculosis medicines and essential laboratory inputs, according to the National TB Control Program (PNLT). A July 29, 2026 advocacy meeting gathered civil society, the Club des Amis Damien, patient groups, and parliamentarians to press for increased national health funding for TB. TB now ranks second in Africa after Nigeria; 2025 saw a drop in case notifications due to stockouts of diagnostics and drugs. For the second half of 2026, approximately 157,000 adults and 14,000 children with TB require treatment, but current stocks are insufficient, risking ~98,000 adults and 2,984 children missing medications. Global Fund support would cover only part of needs (meds: 46/106 million; labs: 14/81 million). From 2028, GF will fund 14 of 26 provinces, risking provincial stockouts and undermining universal health coverage, with warnings that interruptions could worsen transmission, fatalities, and drug resistance.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Butembo: two children declared cured leave the Katwa Ebola Treatment Center.
article.articleSummary: Two children, ages 11 months and 4 years, were declared cured of Ebola and discharged from Katwa Ebola Treatment Center in Butembo, North Kivu, on July 30. They had tested positive a week earlier and presented with fever, vomiting, and diarrhea; after initial care at local health posts, they received a week of treatment at the Katwa CTE. Families praised the care and urged others with Ebola-like symptoms to seek prompt treatment to improve survival. The discharge follows a week after four Katwa patients left the center: three were cured, and a fourth suspected case tested negative in laboratory analyses. One cured patient was a nurse who contracted Ebola while caring for an infected patient unknowingly. Butembo remains the epicenter of the 17th Ebola outbreak in North Kivu, with 220 confirmed cases in the city and 325 in the province as of July 27, totaling about 3,360 cases in two and a half months.

article.articleHeadline: Ituri: the synergy of stakeholders, an essential response to the Ebola outbreak (incident manager of the response) - ACP
article.articleSummary: On July 31, 2026, in Bunia, Ituri province, northeast Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ebola virus disease response, led by new incident manager Dr. Steve Ahuka, prioritized strengthened synergy among all actors to accelerate interruption of the transmission chain. Ahuka emphasized that outbreak management requires daily innovation and true unity of action, as no single actor can manage the outbreak alone. The coordination framework provides the government with essential information to guide strategic decisions, bolster field interventions, and contain the outbreak in Ituri. article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Lolwa: Lack of logistics paralyzes the outbreak response - ACP
article.articleSummary: As of July 31, 2026, Ebola in Lolwa health zone, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, is severely hampered by logistics gaps. Medical chief Dr. Patrick Mbarikane says only one motorcycle is operational for the entire Lolwa area, limiting mobility for surveillance, infection prevention and control, risk communication and community engagement, and dignified and safe burials. Since the outbreak began, eight confirmed Ebola cases have been recorded with three deaths; two patients have recovered and returned to their communities (one in Lolwa, one in Pekele). Of ten health areas in the zone, three are affected, with Pekele and Lolwa hosting active transmission foci; Lolwa houses the main reference hospital. Poor telecommunications coverage in seven health areas impedes real-time data transmission, and there is a risk of stockouts of essential PCI and EDS supplies. article.articleHeadline: Traveling in Europe? Also watch out for this tick-borne disease.

article.articleHeadline: Teeth can't chew it, stomach acid can't kill it! This is how Trichinella spiralis invades the human body, step by step.
article.articleSummary: Trichinella spiralis infection (trichinellosis) is transmitted when cysts in raw or undercooked pork and other meats survive chewing and gastric acid, releasing larvae that invade skeletal muscles. In humans, adult worms mature in the small intestine within 2–3 days; females release new larvae 5–7 days after infection, which travel via blood and lymph to muscles, forming cysts that persist unless calcified. Affected regions include China’s Yunnan, Tibet, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hubei, Henan, Liaoning, Jilin and Heilongjiang, with deaths mainly in the Southwest. Clinical phases span incubation to acute disease and recovery; fever, myalgias, edema, and diarrhea are common, while severe cases can cause myocarditis or encephalitis. Diagnosis relies on muscle biopsy showing cysts; serology aids confirmation. Prevention centers on thorough cooking to at least 70°C for 10 minutes, freezing at −15°C for 20 days, avoiding cross-contamination, and consuming only inspected meats; seek medical care for post-meat fever or muscle pain.

article.articleHeadline: Tiny RNAs Linked to COVID-19 Heart Damage

article.articleSummary: Arboviruses: France's Santé publique France reports minor autochthonous dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile virus infections from May 1 to July 26, 2026, with substantial imported cases across 13 regions. By July 27, 2026, two autochthonous dengue cases were identified in Tarn and Hérault (Occitanie), and one autochthonous chikungunya case in Tarn—the first chikungunya circulation detected in metropolitan France in 2026. Two autochthonous West Nile virus infections were confirmed in Pyrénées-Orientales (Occitanie) and Bouches-du-Rhône (PACA). Imported totals: 87 chikungunya, 261 dengue, 9 Zika. Import sources: chikungunya from Mauritius, French Guiana, Mayotte; dengue from Martinique, Togo, French Polynesia; Zika from Indonesia, Cameroon, Congo. Imported cases span 13 regions, including Île-de-France, Occitanie, Nouvelle-Aquitaine, and PACA.

article.articleHeadline: Baricuatro: Clean up, stay alert against dengue
article.articleSummary: 2026-07-31 update: Cebu Province reports 381 confirmed dengue cases and 2 deaths amid persistent rains, with hospitals on heightened alert and fast lanes for prompt treatment. Governor Pamela Baricuatro urged the public, especially parents, to clean surroundings to prevent dengue-carrying mosquitoes from breeding in clean but stagnant water, noting that even small amounts of standing water can serve as breeding grounds. Residents with dengue-like symptoms should seek prompt medical attention for evaluation. Symptoms include severe abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding from the nose or gums, difficulty breathing, and fatigue. The message emphasizes vigilance and proactive prevention to avert severe illness and reduce transmission.

triage.headline_ja: バリクアトロ知事:清掃と警戒を呼びかけ、デング熱対策

article.articleHeadline: Capitol assures adequate antibiotic supply amid leptospirosis threat
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis remains a public health concern in Cebu, Philippines, with provincial hospitals reporting an adequate doxycycline stock for treatment as of July 31, 2026. Health officials warn that persistent rains raise floodwater–borne infection risk, as contaminated water may carry bacteria from rat and other animal urine. Transmission occurs through cuts, or via eyes, nose or mouth. Incubation ranges from 2 to 30 days after exposure. Symptoms include high fever, headache, muscle and back pain, red eyes, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain; jaundice, breathing difficulty or reduced urination may signal severe illness. Residents are advised to avoid walking or swimming in floodwaters; if unavoidable, wear waterproof boots and gloves, cover wounds with waterproof bandages, and wash exposed skin promptly with soap and clean water. Do not self-medicate; doxycycline should be taken only under doctor’s prescription after medical consultation to prevent complications.

article.articleHeadline: One more imported dengue fever case; the patient had been to the Philippines.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 July 2026, Hong Kong reported one more imported dengue fever case, with travel to the Philippines during the incubation period, in the 24–30 July reporting week. The year-to-date dengue total is 27 cases (25 imported, 2 locally acquired). In 2023 there were 59 cases (all imported); in 2024 there were 161 cases (156 imported, 5 local). Two imported chikungunya fever cases have been recorded this year. The Centre for Health Protection notes that warm, rainy summer conditions favor Aedes mosquito breeding, and authorities remind residents to maintain environmental hygiene to reduce transmission risk.

triage.triage_reason: 香港での輸入症例1例の報告であり、既知の疾患・既知の伝播パターンで、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 香港の輸入症例報告が主題だが、感染発生地はフィリピンであるため対象国としてPhilippinesを記載。China/Hong Kongは輸入例の報告地であり発生地ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Chikungunya under control in Samar, Philippines: Health officials
article.articleSummary: Chikungunya cases in Samar province, Philippines, are under control as of 2026-07-31. The DOH Eastern Visayas Regional Epidemiology and Surveillance Unit reports 372 chikungunya cases, mainly from Basey and Gandara, with no new surge observed. Sporadic cases persist in various parts of the region, but the number of new infections is not considered alarming, according to Roderick Cerro, head of the EV-RESU. Chikungunya is transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Typical symptoms include abrupt fever and severe joint pain, often with muscle pain, headache, nausea, fatigue, and rash. Severe joint pain can last days to months or longer; serious complications are uncommon, though atypical severe cases can cause long-term symptoms or death in older adults and infants under one year. There is no specific antiviral cure; treatment is supportive.

triage.headline_ja: フィリピン・サマール州、チクングニア熱は制御下にあると保健当局
triage.triage_reason: 372症例が報告されているが当局は「制御下」「新規急増なし」と評価しており、深刻な公衆衛生上の懸念や異常性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue cases surge in Cebu
article.articleSummary: Dengue cases surge in Cebu as of Jan 1–Jul 18: Cebu City reports 1,228 dengue cases and 10 deaths, CFR 0.81%. The rise prompts intensified monitoring by Cebu City and Cebu Provincial health offices during the rainy season. The figure is a 12.35% increase from 1,093 cases in the same period in 2025. Dengue fatalities rose from 3 to 10 year-to-date. Patients span ages 2 months to 96 years, with a median of 12. In children 1–10 years old, 498 cases (40.55%) were recorded. Males account for 661 cases (53.83%). Data derive from the Cebu City Epidemiology Surveillance and Statistics Unit (CESSU) of the City Health Department. The report highlights ongoing dengue activity in Cebu City during the current surveillance period.

triage.notes: デング熱は毎年フィリピンの雨季に流行する疾患であり、地方自治体レベルでの監視強化対応が行われている。国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威としての性質は低いが、死亡率上昇の推移は注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Leopard Attack in Barwani: 9-Year-Old Boy Dies 21 Days Later, Rabies Suspected
article.articleSummary: Leopard attack in Barwani district, Madhya Pradesh, on July 7 left nine-year-old Kunal dead 21 days later amid rabies suspicion. Kunal and Arun (10) were grazing goats in Moharat Mal village, Bijasan area near the MP–Maharashtra border when they inadvertently entered a leopard’s resting site. Both were rescued and treated at Civil Hospital Sendhwa and later MY Hospital Indore, and discharged on July 22. Kunal died on July 28; officials are awaiting laboratory confirmation on rabies as a contributing factor. If rabies is confirmed, the forest department will sanitise the area and proceed with leopard rescue along standard wildlife and public health protocols. The health department has not yet shared the cause of death; the next steps depend on lab results.

article.articleHeadline: Waste collection halted, foul odor during rain and increased risk of infection.
article.articleSummary: Patna, Bihar, India, is confronting a sanitation crisis as about 4,700 contract sanitation workers and drivers are on an indefinite strike for the second day, halting garbage collection across the city. Ongoing heavy rains have left uncollected waste in streets and dustbins for 48 hours, generating a foul odor and raising the risk of infectious diseases such as dengue, malaria, and diarrhea. The hardest-hit areas include Boring Road, Nehru Nagar, Anandpuri, SK Puri, Shivpuri, Rajiv Nagar, AG Colony, Patel Nagar, Shastrinagar, Rajendra Nagar, Kankarbagh, Mahendru, and Sultan Ganj. Protests at six zonal offices disrupted waste transport by e-rickshaws and large vehicles. Striking workers demand permanent status for daily wage/contract staff, equal pay for equal work, social security, health insurance, ESIC, and compensation for accidents; officials report mobilizing permanent staff, but cleanliness remains far from normal. The disruption also affects Nalanda, Muzaffarpur, and other Bihar districts.

triage.notes: 記事はビハール州パトナ市における衛生労働者のストライキとゴミ収集停止による衛生状態悪化、感染症リスク増加の懸念を報じているが、実際の感染症症例数や発生状況の報告はない。

article.articleHeadline: Indian strain of dengue-vector mosquito may develop resistance to common insecticide: Study - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: Indian Aedes aegypti population in India shows early signs of developing resistance to α-cypermethrin, a common dengue-vector insecticide. A Frontiers in Tropical Diseases study using lab-bred Indian mosquitoes reports 97.91% mortality at the diagnostic dose, signaling potential resistance emergence rather than confirmed, lasting resistance. The research identifies β-esterase as the primary detoxification enzyme, with activity rising more than 21-fold after exposure and binding strongly to insecticide molecules, enabling defense against α-cypermethrin. Resistance may be reversible if the insecticide is not used, and cross-resistance to similar insecticides remains a concern. Findings are specific to the studied lab population and may differ in other populations or natural conditions. Recommendations include insecticide rotation, elimination of breeding sites, and biological control to preserve effectiveness.

triage.headline_ja: インドのデング熱媒介蚊がよく使われる殺虫剤に耐性を発達させる可能性:研究

triage.notes: 本記事は実験室内での蚊の殺虫剤耐性研究であり、実際のデング熱アウトブレイクや症例報告ではない。将来的な媒介対策への影響を示唆する基礎研究情報として位置づけられる。

article.articleHeadline: Bhandari hosts vector-borne disease awareness drive
article.articleSummary: Vector-borne disease awareness drive held in Bhandari on July 30 under NVBDCP, with the theme 'Fight the Bite, Defeat Vector Borne Diseases.' Extra Assistant Commissioner Kilangtemsu and NVBDCP officials Dr. Imnapokim and Dr. Imkongtemsu Longchar outlined transmission, symptoms, prevention, and treatment of malaria, dengue, and Japanese encephalitis, noting Bhandari's climate favors mosquito breeding and urging shared responsibility and proper use of government-supplied anti-mosquito materials. HPV vaccine benefits, including prevention of cervical cancer and protecting young girls’ health, were highlighted by Dr. Imkongtemsu Longchar. The program, chaired by Dr. Lichamo K. Tungoe, Dental Surgeon CHC Bhandari, was attended by members of the Bhandari Town Council, Lotha Hoho, GBs, church leaders, villagers and health workers, and supported by the district administration and medical department. The event took place at Bhandari Town Hall.

article.articleHeadline: Researchers warn: The closed Strait of Hormuz could lead to a biological superspreader event.
article.articleSummary: Hundreds of stranded ships in the Strait of Hormuz risk becoming hubs for microbes, algae, and invertebrates, potentially triggering a biological superspreader event as vessels resume travel. Biofouling accelerates when ships lie idle for more than 10 days, compromising hull coatings and enabling rapid colonization. Invasive species could disrupt local ecosystems by outcompeting native species and by spreading diseases not present in recipient waters. A study published July 22, led by Mario Tamburri of the University of Maryland Center for Climate Research, warns the global maritime network could disseminate these organisms if ships are not cleaned before departure. Mitigations include in-water hull cleaning prior to leaving Hormuz, per-ship risk assessments, and port monitoring in high-risk locations—especially ports with Gulf-region conditions in Greece, the Netherlands, India, and the Middle East.

triage.notes: 記事は船舶停滞による生物付着（藻類・無脊椎動物・微生物）が海洋生態系に与える将来リスクについての研究であり、実際のヒト感染症アウトブレイクではない。インドは高リスク港の一例として言及されているのみで、実際の発生事例ではないためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: Mumbai: ELISA Machine Defunct For 3 Months At Kandivali BMC Hospital Amid Monsoon Disease Surge
article.articleSummary: During Mumbai’s peak monsoon, Kandivali’s Bharat Ratna Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar (BDBA) Hospital has had an ELISA machine non-functional for at least three months, hindering confirmatory testing for dengue, leptospirosis, Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C. In the absence of ELISA, suspected dengue and leptospirosis cases are diagnosed with rapid tests, but BMC surveillance counts only ELISA or RT-PCR confirmations, so many cases are not logged as confirmed. Hospital sources say seven to eight patients recently tested positive for dengue via rapid tests; some cases have been referred to private labs for ELISA at Rs 2,500–4,000 per test. A newly donated ELISA machine, provided by Union Minister Piyush Goyal three months ago, remained non-operational but is now installed and expected to be operational by Saturday. Dr Ajay Gupta says treatment remains unchanged; officials warn that surveillance is hampered by staff shortages and technicians’ limited travel between civic hospitals.

article.articleHeadline: Nipah patient's condition improves, shifted to ward
article.articleSummary: Nipah virus patient: 43-year-old man from Feroke, Kochi (Kerala). Condition improved; shifted to a ward from ICU on Friday after stabilization. Conscious and eating normally. Admitted to Kozhikode Govt Medical College Hospital on June 11 following acute encephalitis and severe respiratory distress, with exposure suspected from cleaning a bat-infested warehouse. Received experimental monoclonal antibody therapy plus supportive care. After two consecutive negative Nipah tests, he was moved from the isolation unit to a transit ICU on July 7. Health officials traced 77 contacts, with dozens closely monitored (family and healthcare workers); all contacts tested negative. The report details the treatment course and successful de-escalation of care amid ongoing Nipah vigilance in the region.

triage.headline_ja: ニパウイルス感染患者の容体改善、一般病棟へ移動
triage.triage_reason: Nipahウイルスは致死率が高く公衆衛生上重篤かつ稀な感染症であり、IHR基準の『深刻な影響』『異常性』の2点に該当するため、フルリスク評価への移行が妥当と判断される。
triage.notes: 本記事は既知のNipahウイルス感染患者(ケララ州フェロケ在住の43歳男性)の回復・病棟移動を報じる続報。接触者77名は全員陰性で、現時点で新規感染拡大の兆候はないが、Nipahは高致死率かつ稀な人獣共通感染症であり、ケララ州では過去にも複数回のアウトブレイクが発生しているため引き続き注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Human Rights Commission sends notice to the state government over malaria-related deaths in Chhattisgarh.
article.articleSummary: Malaria deaths in Kanker district, Chhattisgarh, have reached five within 13 days, according to media reports cited by India’s National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), which on July 31, 2026, took suo motu cognizance and issued a notice to the state government seeking a detailed report within two weeks. The reports also mention an 11-year-old child who died on July 28; an initial malaria test by a private lab was negative, but the child deteriorated and, after transfer to Albelapara hospital, a blood test confirmed malaria too late for survival. If the facts are accurate, NHRC said this would constitute a serious human rights violation. Following the incident, the state health department launched door-to-door malaria screening and community awareness campaigns in the affected areas.

triage.notes: マラリアはインドの一部地域で流行が続く疾患であり、今回の事例は国際的拡大リスクは低いが、診断遅延による死亡例と人権委員会の介入が報告されており、国内の公衆衛生対応状況を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Contaminated water remains a challenge in Haryana villages - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: As of 1 August 2026, Haryana faces widespread drinking-water contamination. About 1,698 of roughly 19,000 samples tested in 2026-27 were contaminated, with total coliform detected in 855 villages. Chemical contaminants include total hardness (87 samples), total dissolved solids (78), fluoride (58), sulfate (26), chloride (23), total alkalinity (11), turbidity (4), iron (3) and nitrate (2). In Kaithal’s Sajuma village, several residents developed hepatitis-A and typhoid, with a suspected death of a minor girl; Faridabad and Kaithal have seen related incidents, and Chanot village in Hisar protested the Bhakra water supply’s quality. Groundwater, often used when canal water is insufficient, shows excessive fluoride. Protests link Bhakra water diversions to Yamuna command areas with tail-end shortages in Adampur block, Hisar. Sirsa district recorded 295 bacteriological failures (183 in Sirsa town). PHED states clean potable water has been restored in Kaithal, with the contaminated tubewell source closed.

triage.headline_ja: ハリヤナ州の村落で汚染水問題が依然として課題に - The Tribune
triage.triage_reason: インドのハリヤナ州で水質汚染による散発的なA型肝炎・腸チフス症例（死亡疑い1件含む）が報告されているが、地方自治体が対応中で規模・拡大性に関する情報が不足しているため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 地元報道による水質汚染問題であり、インド国内の複数村落（Sajuma, Faridabad, Kaithal, Chanotなど）で発生。PHEDにより一部地域では対応済み（清潔な水供給を回復）。国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す情報はなく、継続的な水質管理の問題として注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Malaria in Myanmar threatens to spiral out of control to such an extent that no medicine can cope with it.
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Myanmar's conflict-wracked Karen State is surging as war disrupts health services and drives displacement, with cross-border spillover to Bangladesh and Thailand. Field hospitals report rising cases: 298 in 2025 and 16 in the first quarter of 2026, mostly treated locally amid bombardments. Researchers from SMRU and MORU note a tripling of Plasmodium vivax and a twelvefold rise in Plasmodium falciparum between 2020–2024, signaling intensified transmission and drug resistance. The public health system has collapsed after COVID-19, the 2021 coup, and ongoing conflict, with aid programs paused or scaled back. Myanmar remains a major reservoir for resistant malaria, historically including chloroquine and artemisinin resistance that spread regionally. Abbott Bioline rapid tests have yielded false negatives, undermining detection and highlighting reliance on ACT-based therapies, which previously reduced malaria burden before the upheaval.

triage.headline_ja: ミャンマーのマラリアが制御不能なほど深刻化し、薬剤耐性が進行している
triage.triage_reason: ミャンマー・カレン州で紛争により保健システムが崩壊し、薬剤耐性マラリア（P. falciparum 12倍増）が拡大、タイ・バングラデシュへの越境拡散も報告されており、IHR基準複数該当かつWPRO基準全項目で懸念あり。
triage.notes: バングラデシュへの越境拡散も記載されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。薬剤耐性マラリアの地域拡散リスクが高く、継続的なモニタリングとフルRRAが推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: Zambia : UNICEF Donates K2 Million For Detection Of Viral Haemorrhagic Fevers
article.articleSummary: As of 31 July 2026, UNICEF donated two million Kwacha worth of infection prevention supplies and water, sanitation and hygiene equipment to Zambia to bolster detection of viral haemorrhagic fevers such as Ebola, during a Lusaka handover. The Ministry of Health’s Permanent Secretary for Technical Services, Kennedy Lishimpi, framed the gift as preparedness to prevent VHFs from crossing borders, rather than merely reacting to threats. UNICEF also plans to deliver 150 ambulance vehicles by the end of September (50 already in the country) and a consignment of 200 vaccine refrigerators, strengthening rapid response and cold-chain capacity. UNICEF Country Representative Saja Abdullah stressed preparedness to protect health workers, communities and essential services. The partnership underpins enhanced surveillance, outbreak readiness, and timely containment.

article.articleHeadline: Africa CDC flags constraints on DR Congo's Ebola response as Uganda shows progress
article.articleSummary: DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak, declared May 15, has 3,442 confirmed cases and 1,521 deaths (case fatality rate >44%), with 48 health zones across five provinces, making it the fastest-growing outbreak and second-largest by total cases. Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya warned of mounting constraints hampering the response, including limited contact tracing, rising community transmission and deaths, insufficient bed capacity, funding shortages, insecurity, unsafe burials, and infections among health workers. Progress includes 19 laboratories active (up from 2) and daily testing capacity over 3,000. Bundibugyo-strain therapeutics trials have been launched. Uganda has contained the outbreak and was declared over, credited to leadership and health workers. Africa CDC urged continued vigilance and lifting U.S. entry restrictions on Uganda. Other high-risk countries: South Sudan, Rwanda, Kenya, Zambia, Central African Republic, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Angola, Republic of the Congo, Burundi, Somalia. Visit to Bunia Aug. 2 with the WHO DG.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカCDC、コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ対応における制約を指摘、ウガンダは進展を示す

triage.notes: ザンビア、中央アフリカ共和国、タンザニア、エチオピア、アンゴラ、ブルンジ、ソマリア等は「高リスク国」として言及されているのみで、実際の発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外。ウガンダは流行終息宣言済みだが対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Is there a resurgence of COVID-19 cases? Recommendation: Stop consuming these four things to protect your lungs.
article.articleSummary: Rising respiratory symptoms and a suspected resurgence of COVID-19 are discussed alongside four foods that may quietly harm lung health. In Hanoi, 185 COVID-19 cases were recorded in the past week across 76 wards, nearly doubling the prior week, bringing year-to-date totals to 588 with no deaths reported. The Hanoi CDC notes increased hospitalizations (18 patients at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases), mainly among the elderly or those with underlying conditions; common symptoms include fever, headache, fatigue, cough, sore throat, and diarrhea/nausea. The Ministry of Health urges precaution as summer travel and gatherings raise transmission risk. The piece cautions that even mild COVID-19 can damage lung mucosa and that recovery may be prolonged if diet worsens lung inflammation. It identifies four harmful foods, detailing the first two: excessive sugar/sweets and fried/oily foods; the article truncates before describing the remaining two. Suggests lighter proteins and water during recovery.

article.articleHeadline: More than VND 3.6 trillion needed to sustain the malaria elimination target by 2030
article.articleSummary: On 31 July 2026, Vietnam’s National Institute of Malariology, Parasitology and Entomology (NIMPE) organized a conference in Vũng Tàu ward, Ho Chi Minh City, to safeguard the malaria prevention and elimination program. To achieve full elimination by 2030, Vietnam needs about 3,658.5 billion VND (roughly 3.6 trillion) from 2026–2030, prioritizing surveillance maintenance, research and development, and preventing reintroduction in eliminated areas. By mid-2026, 26 of 34 provinces/cities had achieved malaria elimination, with cases falling 97.76% from 2014–2024 and 246 cases in 2025. However, a double risk persists: 77% of early-2026 cases were imported, mainly from Africa; drug resistance and vector changes; and shrinking international funding. Proposed measures include PCR-based detection of hidden cases, prophylaxis for high-risk groups, and sustained local leadership and digital health, alongside WHO criteria requiring 36 months with no indigenous cases and 5–10 years of preparedness.

article.articleHeadline: 7-year-old girl contracts mumps from her father
article.articleSummary: In Hanoi, Vietnam, a 7-year-old girl contracted mumps from her father, with Mumps IgM positive at Tam Anh General Hospital Hanoi. The four-member family includes grandmother, father, mother, and daughter; the father was diagnosed about 10 days earlier, with no identified source. The child presented with fever up to 39°C and bilateral parotid swelling; she had not received the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine. Mother and grandmother were asymptomatic. Mumps is an acute viral illness spread mainly via respiratory droplets and close contact, especially in shared living spaces; those without immunity are at higher risk. The child received supportive care (antipyretics, analgesics, anti-inflammatory) and rest, improved after three days, and was discharged without complications. Incubation is 12–25 days (average 16–18). Close contacts warrant about 25 days of monitoring; vaccination with MMR is advised, and infected individuals should limit contact with young children, pregnant women, and the immunocompromised, use masks, cover coughs, and maintain hygiene.

triage.notes: 個別家庭内での散発的なおたふく風邪感染事例で、患児は回復し合併症なく退院。公衆衛生上の緊急性は低く、集団感染や地域的流行の兆候は記事内に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Peak of the summer vacation season... Infectious diseases to watch out for by country?
article.articleSummary: Singapore and Taiwan are flagged for dengue fever and Zika virus infections; mosquito-borne diseases can mimic flu-like symptoms, but without timely treatment may cause organ failure or hemorrhagic complications with up to ~20% fatality risk. Protection focuses on wearing light-colored clothing and applying insect repellent every 3–4 hours. Vietnam, Thailand, and Malaysia face ongoing mosquito-borne diseases and measles outbreaks; measles is highly contagious, with fever, rash, cough, and runny nose. Travelers should be vaccinated at least two weeks before departure; if not vaccinated, monitor for symptoms after return and seek prompt medical care to prevent spread. The Philippines is a designated cholera quarantine area, so vigilance around contaminated water and seafood is advised. In the United States and parts of China, avian influenza has human infection risk zones, so avoid farm visits and animal contact. Japan and Hong Kong are not quarantine zones but require strong personal hygiene and awareness of heat-related illness during hot, humid summer.

triage.triage_reason: 既知の季節性感染症（デング熱、麻疹、コレラ、鳥インフルエンザ等）に関する旅行者向け一般的注意喚起記事であり、新規アウトブレイクや異常事態の報告ではないため。
triage.notes: 本記事は特定の新規発生事象を報じるものではなく、夏季旅行者向けに複数国・複数疾患の既知の流行状況をまとめた一般的な健康注意喚起記事である。フィリピンのコレラ検疫区域指定、米国・中国の鳥インフルエンザヒト感染リスク地域等の情報は既存の公衆衛生情報の再掲と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: 'Shield' protects farmers from tuberculosis in Lang Son Province.
article.articleSummary: Proactive community-based screening in Lang Son Province, Vietnam, has protected farmers from tuberculosis (TB) via local health networks. In 2025, Lang Son Lung Hospital organized TB screening in four districts (Lộc Bình, Hữu Lũng, Văn Lãng, Bình Gia), examining 8,640 people, with chest X-rays performed on all and GeneXpert testing for 1,181. Detected 64 drug-susceptible TB cases, 1 pediatric TB case, and 1 drug-resistant TB case. In the first half of 2026, 89% of target individuals were screened; bacteriologically confirmed TB accounted for 76.4%, with 46.6% admissions. Six-month treatment success for bacteriologically confirmed TB reached 91.5%. Drug-resistant TB: 233 Xpert tests, 7 treated (6 Rifampicin-resistant, 1 MDR). Strengthened local capacity via 1 diagnostic/therapy/prevention update training and 3 TB awareness trainings; free medications delivered within 3 km of home, Telehealth, and 78.89% non-cash payments reduced central referrals by 2% year over year.

article.articleHeadline: Controlling disease outbreaks among livestock.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 July 2026, Tuy Quang Province, Vietnam, is contending with H5N1 avian influenza outbreaks in poultry and African swine fever (ASF). H5N1 outbreaks have struck poultry in Viet Lam, Dong Tam, and Tan Quang, with 1,060 birds dead or culled (weight >1,400 kg). Tan Quang declared an outbreak on 22 July. Authorities maintain checkpoints, sanitation, and vaccination; 12,700 doses of avian influenza vaccine have been administered, with a plan to reach over 80% coverage for ring vaccination around affected areas; 482 L disinfectant and 8,290 kg lime used in decontamination; 2,000 kg lime powder and 50 L disinfectant procured for Viet Lam. A violation in Viet Lam led to seizure of 25 poultry and 300 eggs. ASF outbreaks from 21–23 July affected seven communes, triggering culling of 57 pigs from 11 households (>2.2 t). 523 L disinfectant and 4,593 kg lime used; tighter controls on transport and slaughter.

article.articleHeadline: Vietnam: Dengue cases rise in Ho Chi Minh City
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever cases in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, reached 995 for the week ending July 27 (week 30), up 20% from the four-week average, according to the Ho Chi Minh City Center for Disease Control (HCDC). Cumulative 2026 dengue cases through week 30 total 23,481. Dengue, caused by a virus spread via Aedes mosquitoes, typically incubates up to 14 days and usually lasts less than a week. Common symptoms include fever, headache, nausea, vomiting, rash, muscle and joint pain, and minor bleeding. Dengue can progress to severe dengue, a medical emergency requiring hospitalization, with potential hemorrhage, shock, organ failure, and death. The report indicates ongoing dengue activity in Ho Chi Minh City and highlights the need for vector control and clinical vigilance during the season. A death toll is not provided in the briefing.
